doc.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Being his own agent and trying not to remain a sideman
summary: He handles all booking himself, tried booking in Europe in the 1980s, and hopes to lead more.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Are you your own business agent? Do you have an agent that sends you work or are you pretty much—
No I function as my business agent, booking agent, PR person, shipping clerk, roadie, and everything else. And I’m not good at most of those functions.
A lot of musicians have trouble with the areas that need to be taken care of outside their playing. It’s hard.

Well there’s few of us that — anybody like that is interested in. So nobody’s interested in booking Scott Robinson or producing. You know anything I’m going to do, other than answering the phone and going to play with this orchestra or that band, anything beyond © Hamilton Fillius Archive -11-

that either I’m going to do it or it’s not going to happen. So most of the time it doesn’t happen. But every once in a while — I went through a phase in the ‘80s of really getting on the phone and booking myself in Europe and stuff like that. And I had some scary experiences and I got a little bit frightened away from that. And now I’m trying to gingerly sort of get back to the stage of trying to not just be a sideman the rest of my life. I think I’m starting to come out of my shell a little bit. Maybe the giant saxophone is going to help me with that.
Sounds like an album title, doesn’t it?
Scott and his Giant Sax — it sounds like a kid’s book Scott and his Giant Saxophone.
